import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I've written the plan and submitted it for your approval; nothing has been changed in either repo yet. It's a single medium tale called **"`.` at an item start types `@` in capture"**.

**Why the leading `.` stays a dot:** bob's rule that turns `.` into `@` only fires after body text plus a space or tab. Its position check rejects a `.` at position 0 or at a line start, so `bob capture-rewrite --cursor 1 -- '.'` leaves the dot alone. A bare `@` already opens route completion there, and `;` already turns into `:` at the same "item start" positions, so `.` is the odd one out.

**Part 1, bob-cli:**
- Let the `.` → `@` rule also fire when the `.` starts an item: the start of the draft, any later blank-line item, or after leading spaces on an item's first line. It still needs `@` to open route completion there.
- Add a new typing-tip lesson, `route_item_start` ("at an item start"), so typing `@` there teaches `.`.
- Update the unit, tip and CLI tests, the help text and the docs. There's no grammar bump.

**Part 2, Bob Mac Capture:** with only the bob change, a fast `..` at the very start of the draft would give `@.` instead of a literal `.`. The Mac code that undoes the alias on a second dot is never set up at position 0, and its fast-typing check only looks for a space before the caret. The plan:
- lets that undo, and the Space/Escape restores, work at position 0;
- extends the fast-typing check to item starts, for `.` only;
- registers the new tip lesson;
- adds tests and updates the four docs pages that currently say "item-start `.bashrc`/`.5` stay literal", without pushing any page past its word cap.

**Scope I chose myself:** bullet and checkbox starts (`- .`, `- [ ] .`) keep their current behavior, matching how `;` already works. A literal leading dot (`.bashrc`, `.5`) is typed with a fast `..`.

**Decision for you:** one memory toggle, defaulting to yes. It rewrites one bullet in the Capture Alias glossary entry, which would otherwise wrongly say `.` → `@` only works after body text.
